title: Closed-Loop Systems
subtitle: Measure, process, feed back, adapt
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating closed-loop systems within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain closed-loop systems without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in closed-loop systems.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to closed-loop systems.

sections.explainSimply: A closed loop measures a signal, decides whether it meets a rule and changes feedback immediately.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: The loop includes sensor quality, signal processing, feature extraction, threshold logic, feedback latency and learner response. Failure in any link changes what is actually being trained.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Latency, filtering and window length determine temporal precision. Systems should document algorithms sufficiently for replication and safety review.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A driving instructor who gives immediate dashboard feedback while the learner practises a controllable skill.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand closed-loop systems to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: A sophisticated display cannot compensate for a contaminated signal.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using closed-loop systems predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: A sophisticated display cannot compensate for a contaminated signal. Evidence classification: established engineering principle.

Protocol choice requires no outcome measurement
Artifact is irrelevant once feedback begins
quizBank.explanation: A closed loop measures a signal, decides whether it meets a rule and changes feedback immediately.

quizBank.question: Which limitation matters most when interpreting Closed-Loop Systems?
options: A sophisticated display cannot compensate for a contaminated signal.
quizBank.explanation: A sophisticated display cannot compensate for a contaminated signal.

quizBank.question: How should the evidence for Closed-Loop Systems be communicated?
options: As established engineering principle, with methods and outcomes specified
As conclusively effective for all clients
By promising normalisation of the brain
quizBank.explanation: The appropriate evidence label is: established engineering principle.
